segments.text: In this video, we're going to talk about trial balance reports in Dynamics SL and then look at how you can print similar reports in Business Central. In SL, I've printed out the detailed trial balance for a specific period of time and included all accounts.

I can easily see balance information that was posted to each account and sub-account. In addition to the detailed trial balance, I've also printed out the aged AR, allowing me to see aged information for each of my customers and drill into my customers that have balances that I need to collect on.

Now let's look at Business Central and how we can view and print similar trial balance reports. To navigate to the trial balance reports for general ledger, we'll select the search icon and enter in trial balance.
In the available options to select, you can see how both the trial balance, which is similar to the summary trial balance in SL, as well as the detailed trial balance.

In the detailed trial balance report options window, I've indicated that I would like a new page per GL account. Also, in the filter area, you can filter to a specific account or a range of accounts, similar to how you would in SL.
Now let's preview the report and see how the information looks. Here I can see the balance information as well as the detailed transactions posted to the account.
I can scroll through the report and see each account is printed on a new page. Now let's look at the summary trial balance. The summary trial balance report has some different options to select from.

I have the ability to compare values from last year or if I have configured budgets in Business Central, I could compare to the balance that would have been budgeted. Below, I've selected to include actual and comparison balances and display the variance as a percentage.
I'm also rounding to the nearest dollar. Again, I can filter to a specific range of accounts as well as enter a new date range for the report.
You can see on the summary trial balance how it compares this year's balance to last year's as well as displaying the variance as a percentage.
Next, let's look at the age reports for customers. In the search field, I will type aged accounts. In the list, you can see both the AP and AR aging reports.
If I select the aging report option for AR, similar to SL, I can select a date that I want to age the report and if I want the age by transaction date or due date.

I can select the report in detail. I can also filter report to a specific customer class. Now, I can view the aging information for each customer and focus on a specific customer or customers with balances overdue.
In addition to previewing the report in the screen, I could also send the report to PDF or Word. Let's look at what it would look like if it was in Excel.
I'll mark the print to Excel option and preview the report again. In Excel, I can easily perform additional analysis or create different visuals for the data.
And that's a look at trial balance reports in Business Central. To learn more about Business Central, see the following resources.
